licenses.note: The port recreates JEI's item list and carries the reference's MIT notice; JEI's own LICENSE.txt covers the name and the drawing it recreates.

licenses.name: MIT
licenses.note: The reference, JEI 18.0.0.66 for 1.20.6, is MIT (Copyright (c) 2014-2015 mezz). The commit is the last of the 1.20.6 line, 20 commits past the v18.0.0 tag, and the published 18.0.0.66 build lists it as its newest change.

deviations.what: The list is not drawn on a grug mod's own container screens; it is drawn on the player's inventory and on every other container screen, vanilla or another mod's, that is not a GrugScreen.
deviations.why: The first version targets the screens the issue names, and drawing on a mod's own GrugScreen would change that mod's GUI goldens. JEI draws its list on every container screen.

deviations.what: The list is paged with the back and next buttons, which are drawn as plain highlight boxes without the reference's arrows or page number.
deviations.why: The buttons' look is part of the chrome the first version does not draw.

deviations.what: The search field has no caret movement with the arrows, Home or End, no selection, select-all, cut, copy or paste, no delete key, no undo and no search history, and its caret does not blink. Its box is an outline and not the reference's nine-slice texture, and it has no config button beside it.
deviations.why: The overlay's key pass names the arrows, Home, End and Delete as keys an overlay is not given, and the host has no call for the field's selection or the clipboard.

deviations.what: A search matches the item's name, and a word that starts with @ matches the mod id. The reference's tooltip search (its # prefix, on by default), tag search ($) and the other modes are not there: a # or $ is searched as part of the name. A mod's name is not searched, only its id, and Alpha has no item names, so its words match the registry name.
deviations.why: The host exposes no tooltip lines or tags for an item and no mod display name.

deviations.what: Ctrl+O hides and shows the overlay. The key is fixed and cannot be rebound, and the list is hidden entirely, where JEI keeps drawing its config button while its list is hidden.
deviations.why: The host has no key binding or config API for a mod to register a rebindable key.

deviations.what: Right-clicking an item does not open its uses or recipes, and there are no recipe categories or recipe screen.
deviations.why: The recipe viewer's category, uses and recipes host API is a separate piece of work.

deviations.what: There are no bookmarks, so an item cannot be pinned across screens.
deviations.why: Bookmarks need per-player persistent state, drag input and a second list beside the ingredient list.

deviations.what: There is no plugin API for other mods to register categories or ingredient subtypes, and no configuration screen or file for the mod's options.
deviations.why: A grug mod has no plugin boundary to extend and no configuration file it reads; what a grug mod may extend is a design question.

deviations.what: The items are ordered by registry key on 1.20.6, with the minecraft namespace first and everything else alphabetically, and by numeric item id on 1.2.5, Beta and Alpha, which have no registry key; JEI orders by creative tab and then by mod name. The same item therefore sits at a different place.
deviations.why: A stable key order is what a committed golden needs, and the host exposes no creative tabs; the older versions only have the numeric id, so that is the order they use. JEI's order is recorded as the difference.

deviations.what: The list is one entry per registered item except air, where JEI lists the stacks of the creative tabs: a potion, a splash potion and a lingering potion are separate entries there. The potion, splash and lingering variants, and every other stack that differs only in damage or components, are therefore missing from the port. The operator tab's items (barrier, the command blocks, jigsaw, structure block, structure void, debug stick and light) are hidden from a player who may not use them on 1.20.6, as in the reference.
deviations.why: The host exposes one Item per registry key and no stack with damage or components in the item list, so listing those stacks needs a stack-valued item list and an overlay that draws and gives a stack, which is the remaining piece of this issue.

deviations.what: The list holds items only. JEI registers fluid stacks as a second ingredient type and shows them in the same list, so a fluid such as water or lava is an entry there and is missing here.
deviations.why: The host lists items only and has no fluid call, neither a count and an entry nor a fluid cell to draw, so the fluid list is a separate piece.

deviations.what: Hovering an item draws the reference's highlight but no tooltip, item count or mod name, and the grid draws no page number or config button.
deviations.why: The overlay API has no tooltip callback or item-name source, and the first version draws no chrome beyond the icons and the highlight.

deviations.what: While a left click on the grid would delete the stack on the cursor, the reference hides the hover highlight and shows its delete tooltip ("jei.tooltip.delete.item", "Click to delete.") instead (IngredientGrid.java:130-137,146-153; DeleteItemInputHandler.java:78-81); the port keeps drawing the highlight, and it draws no tooltip of either kind.
deviations.why: The overlay API asks nothing about the click a hover would make and offers no tooltip, so the port marks the hovered cell from the mouse position alone.

deviations.what: The port gives one item on a left or right click and a stack on shift+left or the middle button, into the player's inventory. The reference's default MOUSE_PICKUP give puts the picked stack on the cursor and merges it into a stack the cursor already carries of the same item, up to the item's maximum (ServerCommandUtil.mousePickupItemStack, :137-158). A left click while the cursor carries an item deletes that stack unless the clicked item is the same one, which gives one item instead; an item that cannot stack, such as a tool, a piece of armour, a potion or a filled bucket, is deleted as well, because two of a stack of one never merge. The port has no give-versus-cheat mode and no cheat permission check, and it sends no "Gave ... to ..." chat message. Its give is silent, as the reference's default MOUSE_PICKUP give is: only the reference's hotbar-slot and INVENTORY give paths play the pickup sound.
deviations.why: The overlay host exposes the press's button and whether shift is held, but not JEI's GiveMode setting, its cheat permission, its pickup sound, its chat line, or a way to write the cursor, so a give goes into the inventory where the reference puts the picked stack on the cursor. The delete matches the reference's merge check for an undamaged item, a max-stack-1 item included, since two of a stack of one cannot merge; a carried stack with damage or components is compared by its item id alone, because the host gives the overlay no damage of the cursor's stack, where the reference compares those too.

deviations.what: The item on the cursor is deleted where the reference deletes it, but on a client of a remote server the delete clears only that client's copy of the cursor, while the reference's packet removes the stack the server holds. The give is the half that does reach the server: a client joined to one names the item to it, which puts it in the player's inventory there (#1099).
deviations.why: The cursor a click reads and the delete it makes are calls of the overlay host on the client that draws it, and that client sends the server no cursor write, where the reference's delete packet does. The give had the same gap and now names the item to the server over the test-control channel.
